pr_comment: A consumable's only Use control is a hover-only overlay (`hidden group-hover:block`). Clicking the tile itself sends any non-gear item (Health/Mana Potion, Leather, chest) to setSelectedBlock and closes the inventory. On a device with no hover, potions cannot be drunk, and the tile tap turns a potion into the selected build block.
reasoning:
handleConsume is the only path that calls consumeEffect (grep: GamePanels.jsx:208 is the only caller). Take a touch player on Android Chrome, or a keyboard user, who buys a Health Potion from the merchant. The TradingInterface comment says it is 'usable'. The player opens Character and taps the potion. No hover state is ever shown, so the Use button stays display:none and is not focusable. The tile's onClick (lines 400-407) runs setSelectedBlock('Health Potion') and onClose(). The panel shuts, the potion is not consumed, and the player now holds an item that cannot be placed. There is no other in-game way to drink it. A fix should make Use reachable without hover, for example always visible for consumables or the tile tap consuming a consumable. Tile clicks should only select items that idForBlock can place.

**Verification:** normal. Trigger: a player on a no-hover device (Android Chrome touch, which reaches this panel through the touch tray's `character` button at frontend/src/ui/touchTray.js:15 `action: 'setShowInventory'`), or a keyboard-only player, tries to use a potion.

How it happens, in frontend/src/ui/GamePanels.jsx:
- The Use control sits inside `<div className="absolute top-0.5 right-0.5 hidden group-hover:block z-10">` (line 423). It is display:none until the tile is hovered. A display:none button cannot be focused or tapped.

pr_comment: The Spells tab (MagicSystem) hardcodes each spell's tier-I damage and mana (Fireball 50 DMG / 15 MP, and so on), but casts scale with player level through store.getSpellStats -> game/spellTiers.js spellStatsAt. Past level 2 to 5 the panel shows numbers the cast does not use.
reasoning:
A level-5 player opens Character -> Spells. It shows Fireball "50 DMG / 15 MP" and Lightning "75 DMG / 25 MP". The actual casts (EnhancedMagicSystem resolveCastBaseDamage/resolveCastManaCost) do 120 dmg for 22 MP and 160 dmg for 35 MP. The player under-reads their power and is surprised when mana drains faster than the panel says, which breaks the 'HUD is honest' rule in .claude/rules/game-code.md. Fix: build the rows from spellStatsAt(spell, level) or useGameStore getSpellStats (subscribed to level), not literals, so the panel and the cast read one source.

**Verification:** normal (display-only, but wrong for every player who reaches level 2 or higher). Trigger: a player at level 2 or above opens the Spells panel (MenuSystem.jsx:201-203 renders `<MagicSystem>` when `gameState.showMagic`). In GamePanels.jsx:465-470 the `spells` array is a hardcoded literal: `{ name: 'Fireball', ... damage: 50, mana: 15 }`, `Iceball 40/12`, `Lightning 75/25`, `Arcane 60/18`. Rows render `{spell.damage} DMG` and `{spell.mana} MP` straight from that literal, and the component never reads the store's `level` or `getSpellStats`. Casts, however, use level-scaled values.

pr_comment: The touch hit-targets for action, cast, jump and dodge do not line up with the glyphs that TouchControlsSurface draws. Each glyph is larger and sits higher, so a band along its top/left edge (about 16-24 px on jump and action) is visible but not tappable. Line 223 claims the hit geometry 'mirrors the visible glyphs'.
reasoning:
On an 820x1180 iPad the jump glyph spans bottom calc(12%+104px) to +64px, which is 245-310 px from the bottom (TouchControlsSurface.jsx:224). Its hit-target spans calc(11%+96px) to +60px, which is 226-286 px (line 299). A thumb on the upper third of the visible jump button lands on no data-touch-btn, so the window router treats it as a look-drag and the player does not jump. Action (glyph 92 px at bottom 12%, hit 84 px at 11%), cast (glyph 68 px at right 132 / bottom 10%, hit 64 px at right 124 / bottom 9%) and dodge (glyph right 132 / bottom 10%+90, hit right 124 / bottom 9%+86) have the same mismatch. touch-layout-gates.test.jsx:81-83 says these four are 'not checked'. The Pause control was already fixed for this exact drift (B7). Fix: derive each glyph's and its hit-target's geometry from one shared style function, as the spell row and fan already do, and extend the glyph-drift gate to all four controls.

**Verification:** normal. Trigger: any touch-UI session where the player taps the upper or left edge of the visible jump, action, cast or dodge glyph. The glyph layer is drawn bigger and higher than the hit-targets, so taps on a visible band of each button reach no control.

What each layer draws:
- Glyphs (TouchControlsSurface.jsx):
  - action: `right: +26px, bottom: '12%', 92x92` (l.211)
  - cast: `right: +132px, bottom: '10%', 68x68` (l.216)
  - dodge: `right: +132px, bottom: 'calc(10% + 90px)', 60x60` (l.221)
  - jump: `right: +44px, bottom: 'calc(12% + 104px)', 64x64` (l.224)

pr_comment: The low-health heartbeat never stops when the player dies. damagePlayer sets playerHealth to 0 at death, and lowHealthIntensity(0, max) returns 1 (game/lowHealth.js: `if (ratio <= 0) return 1`). So the bucket goes to 4 and the effect starts the fastest interval, about 0.55 s per beat. Nothing reads isAlive, and the DeathScreen waits for a Respawn click, so the beat repeats under 'YOU DIED' with no end. Fix: count the player as out of danger when dead, either by subscribing to isAlive and forcing bucket 0 when it is false, or by having lowHealthIntensity take an alive flag. Same pattern at 2 sites (HeartbeatAudio.jsx:22, LowHealthVignette.jsx:17).
reasoning:
A player is killed by a mob. damagePlayer (store line ~1045) sets playerHealth to 0 and isAlive to false, and HUD.jsx renders the DeathScreen, which stays until the player taps Respawn. HeartbeatAudio re-renders with health 0, so intensity is 1, bucket is 4 and period is heartbeatPeriod(1) = 0.55 s. The effect plays a beat at once and then calls setInterval(playHeartbeat, 550). Its only stop condition is bucket <= 0, which needs health back above 35%, and that happens only on respawn. A player who leaves the death screen up (reads the stats, steps away, or a touch player whose play stays live at death) hears a frantic 'lub-dub' about twice a second, the near-death danger cue, layered over the defeat sting, for as long as the screen is up. LowHealthVignette has the same missing gate: it keeps its maximum-intensity red pulse running at z 37 under the death screen's 80% black scrim. The heartbeat is documented as a cue for 'while the player's health is critical'.

**Verification:** normal (small, audio-only, but it happens on every death). Trigger: any player death; the frantic heartbeat then loops under the death screen until the player clicks Respawn.

How it happens:
- **Health goes to 0 on death.** In `frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx`, `damagePlayer` sets `playerHealth` to `newHealth = Math.max(0, ...)` (line ~1043). When `newHealth <= 0`, it sets `isAlive: false` (line 1049). Health stays at 0 until `respawn()` (line 1078) restores it to `maxHealth`.

pr_comment: The level-up burst's background is `radial-gradient(circle, rgba(var(--ui-accent), 0.5) 0%, transparent 64%)`. cssVars.js writes --ui-* colours as space-separated channels ('201 168 106'), so this resolves to `rgba(201 168 106, 0.5)`. That mixes the space syntax with a comma alpha, which is invalid CSS, so the whole background declaration is dropped. Fix: `rgb(var(--ui-accent) / 0.5)`, the form tokens.js and the rest of the HUD use.
reasoning:
On every level-up, SimpleLevelUpEffect animates the 'gold radial burst behind the banner', a w-80 h-80 m.div whose only paint is this background. The browser rejects the invalid colour, so the div has no background and the burst never shows. The player gets only the banner text, without the intended gold flash. hexToRgbChannels (cssVars.js:10-16) emits 'r g b', and every other use in the diff is `rgb(var(--ui-x))` or `rgb(var(--ui-x) / a)`. This is the only `rgba(var(--ui-…), …)` site in frontend/src.

**Verification:** nit. Trigger: every level-up, when SimpleLevelUpEffect renders the burst m.div. frontend/src/SimpleExperienceSystem.jsx:134 sets `background: 'radial-gradient(circle, rgba(var(--ui-accent), 0.5) 0%, transparent 64%)'`. applyThemeVars (cssVars.js:68-77) writes every COLOR_VARS entry, `--ui-accent` included (line 32), through hexToRgbChannels (cssVars.js:10-16), and that returns the space-separated form `${r} ${g} ${b}`. After substitution the value becomes `rgba(R G B, 0.5)`, which mixes the modern space syntax with the legacy comma alpha, so it is not a valid colour.

pr_comment: bareKeyRe's negative lookahead (?!\s*:) is meant to exclude dictionary definitions, but it also rejects a key on the true side of a ternary (`cond ? 'key' : ...`). Live keys reached that way are not counted as uses.
reasoning:
game/bossTier.js:39 (`n === 1 ? 'boss.dragonRisen' : 'boss.dragon'`) and MenuSystem.jsx:380 (`t(x ? 'menu.heldStopped' : ...)`) match neither literalCallRe nor bareKeyRe. Each is classified 'fixture' at best, or 'dead' when no test happens to mention it. The no-dead-keys gate (tests/i18n/key-resolution.test.js) would then go red with 'remove from BOTH locales', and scripts/ci/i18n-dead-keys.mjs would list live copy as safe to delete. That is the unrecoverable outcome this file exists to prevent. Fix: tell a definition apart by its position as an object key (preceded by `{` or `,`, followed by `:`), not by any trailing colon.

**Verification:** nit. The trigger is a live key that source reaches only as the true branch of a ternary, which a maintainer could also format with the newline before `:`. Mechanism, from frontend/src/i18n/keyReachability.js:42: `bareKeyRe = (key) => new RegExp(`['"\`]${escapeKey(key)}['"\`](?!\\s*:)`)`. The `(?!\s*:)` cannot distinguish a dictionary entry (`'k': ...`) from a ternary true branch (`? 'k' : ...`), and `\s` also matches newlines. literalCallRe (line 29) requires `t(` right before the quote, so `t(cond ? 'k' : ...)` fails it too.

pr_comment: Player-facing text is hardcoded in English instead of going through t(), so the zh-CN locale shows English in the core panels. TradingInterface also picks its toast colour with `tradeMessage.includes('Not enough')`, which stops working once that message is localized. Fix: move every literal into STRINGS (en and zh-CN), render it with t(), and have TradingInterface keep an ok/fail flag instead of matching on the text. That covers the 14 sites listed. Same pattern at 14 sites (GamePanels.jsx:806, GamePanels.jsx:835, GamePanels.jsx:671, GamePanels.jsx:430, GamePanels.jsx:385, GamePanels.jsx:178, GamePanels.jsx:546, GamePanels.jsx:466, TradingInterface.jsx:26, TradingInterface.jsx:79, TradingInterface.jsx:117, ChestInventoryPanel.jsx:54, SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:63, SpellUpgradePanel.jsx:191).
reasoning:
A player switches to zh-CN with LocaleToggle and opens Settings. They see 'How to Play', 'Manage Worlds', 'Resume Game' and 'Show Stats (F3)' in English. Inventory shows 'Use', 'N Slots', 'Head/Main/Chest...' and 'Compared against equipped:'. Building Tools shows English tool names and descriptions, the Merchant panel shows 'Coins', 'Cost', 'Trade' and English purchase messages, the chest says 'Storage Container Chest', and Talents shows 'Talents', 'Locked', 'Prerequisite:' and 'Rank'. Other strings on the same screens are already translated, so the UI is a mix of two languages. Once someone translates the trade-failure message, the failure toast also turns green ('success'), because its status comes from matching the English text.

**Verification:** nit. Trigger: a player switches to zh-CN with LocaleToggle (LocaleToggle.jsx:13 `setLocale(locale === 'en' ? 'zh-CN' : 'en')`) and opens one of these panels. GamePanels.jsx already imports and uses `useT()` (line 6, line 54 and elsewhere), but some literals skip it. In Settings: line 806 `/> How to Play`, line 816 `/> Manage Worlds`, line 835 `Resume Game` and line 671 `Show Stats (F3)`. Nearby buttons in the same panel are translated, e.g. `{t('credits.button')}` and `{t('panel.footer.settings')}`.

pr_comment: loadCjkFonts sets `_loaded = results.some(Boolean)`, so a run where only one face loads still latches success for the session. The face that failed is never retried. The likeliest partial failure is the large PuHuiTi body face, while the small Smiley Sans display face succeeds.
reasoning:
A player on a flaky connection toggles to zh-CN. Smiley Sans (small) loads, and the large subset puhuiti-regular.woff2 fetch fails. results=[true,false] makes _loaded true, so every later toggle returns early at line 23. All Chinese body text then renders in the system fallback for the rest of the session, which is exactly the 'one transient failure permanently disables the webfont' outcome the comment at lines 28-33 says the latch was rewritten to prevent. It is only prevented when every face fails. Fix: track success per face and retry only the faces that failed, latching only when all have loaded.

**Verification:** nit. Trigger: on the first switch to zh-CN, one of the two FontFace loads fails (for example a transient network error on the large /fonts/puhuiti-regular.woff2) while the other succeeds.

The mechanism is as described. In frontend/src/i18n/cjkFonts.js, line 47 sets `_loaded = results.some(Boolean);`. With results=[true,false] this latches `_loaded = true`, and every later call then hits line 23 (`if (_loaded) return true;`) without retrying the failed face.

pr_comment: `webglInfo` is an IIFE at module scope. It creates a WebGL context, queries WEBGL_debug_renderer_info and then calls loseContext. App.jsx:27 imports this module statically and only the render is gated on `import.meta.env.DEV` (App.jsx:349). Because the IIFE has side effects and package.json declares no `sideEffects` field, the bundler keeps it, so every production boot builds a throwaway GPU context for an overlay that is dev-only.
reasoning:
Every production player, iPad and iPhone included, pays for creating and tearing down an extra WebGL context while the module graph evaluates. That happens before the game canvas makes its own context, and it adds boot time and GPU churn on the devices with the tightest frame and context budgets, for diagnostics no production player can open. On the base branch (UI absent) this does not happen. Fix: compute webglInfo lazily, for example inside handleCopyLogs or a useMemo when the panel opens, or load DebugOverlay through a DEV-only dynamic import so production never evaluates it.

**Verification:** nit. Trigger: every production page load. frontend/src/ui/DebugOverlay.jsx:7-40 declares `const webglInfo = (() => { ... document.createElement('canvas'); canvas.getContext('webgl') ... gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info') ... loseContextExt.loseContext(); })();` at module scope, so it runs as soon as the module is evaluated. App.jsx:27 imports the module statically (`import { DebugOverlay } from './ui/DebugOverlay';`). Only the render is gated: App.jsx:349 has `{import.meta.env.DEV && !hudHidden && <DebugOverlay .../>}`.

pr_comment: The chest transfer tiles' aria-labels give the whole stack count (`Move ${qty} ${item} to chest` / `to backpack`), but each activation calls transferItem(coords, item, 1, ...), which moves exactly one item.
reasoning:
A screen-reader or keyboard player focuses a tile that has 5 Stone. It is announced as "Move 5 Stone to chest". They press Enter, and 1 Stone moves. The tile is then announced as "Move 4 Stone to chest". The control promises a bulk move it never performs, so assistive-tech users misjudge what each press does. The same mismatch is at line 106 for the chest-to-backpack direction. Fix: make the label describe a single-item move (for example "Move 1 of 5 Stone to chest"), or make the action match the label. Either change covers both sites.

**Verification:** nit. Trigger: any screen-reader user who activates a chest or backpack tile holding more than one of an item. In frontend/src/ui/ChestInventoryPanel.jsx line 79 the label is `aria-label={`Move ${qty} ${item} to chest`}`, but lines 75-76 call `transferItem(coords, item, 1, 'to_chest')` for both click and Enter/Space. The store's `transferItem: (coords, item, quantity = 1, direction)` (frontend/src/store/useGameStore.jsx:680-694) moves exactly `quantity` items, so with qty=5 each press moves 1 and the tile is then announced as "Move 4 ...".
